Mr. S.K. Mandal, learned counsel for the petitioner.

2. Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel with Mr. B.S. Koranga,
learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. The petitioner is working with the respondent- Department as "Paryavaran Mitra" in regular establishment with respondent no.3-Chief Medical Officer, Almora.
4. The petitioner was convicted in Sessions Trial No.16 of 2013, State Vs. Vijay @ Brij Lal under Section 376 IPC registered with Police Station J.P. Nagar vide judgment and order dated 14.05.2015.
The petitioner moved an appeal against his conviction and sentence before the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad and he was released on bail on 01.06.2015.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. After his conviction the petitioner was placed under suspension by the order of respondent no.3-Chief Medical Officer, Almora dated 17.05.2016.

6. Grievance of the petitioner is that the petitioner though placed under suspension is not being given Subsistence Allowance and is compelled to file a certificate to this effect that he is not gainfully employed in any trade, business or calling.

7. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is ready to file a notarized affidavit as it is very difficult for him to get any such certificate as asked by the respondent-Department.

8. Per contra, learned State counsel submits that purpose of the Rules whereby certificate of his not being gainfully employed in any trade or calling is asked for, would be served with a notarized affidavit with the Competent Authority-respondent no.3, who placed the petitioner under suspension.

sentences.text: Having considered the submission made by learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, the petitioner is not pressing the relief with regard to quashing of the suspension order, but he limit his relief to the payment of Subsistence Allowance to him by respondent no.3.

10. Petitioner is ready to file an affidavit to this effect that he is not gainfully employed in any trade,
business and calling.
11. The submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner is acceptable.

12. If learned counsel for the petitioner would file a notarized affidavit to this effect that he is not gainfully employed in any trade business or calling, during the period of his suspension, respondent no.3 will consider that affidavit and shall pass an order to pay Subsistence Allowance to the petitioner along with its arrears, as per law, within a period of one month from the date of submission of such affidavit.
13.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
6. Grievance of the petitioner is that the petitioner though placed under suspension is not being given Subsistence Allowance and is compelled to file a certificate to this effect that he is not gainfully employed in any trade, business or calling.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Having considered the submission made by learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, the petitioner is not pressing the relief with regard to quashing of the suspension order, but he limit his relief to the payment of Subsistence Allowance to him by respondent no.3.
10. Petitioner is ready to file an affidavit to this effect that he is not gainfully employed in any trade,
business and calling.
12. If learned counsel for the petitioner would file a notarized affidavit to this effect that he is not gainfully employed in any trade business or calling, during the period of his suspension, respondent no.3 will consider that affidavit and shall pass an order to pay Subsistence Allowance to the petitioner along with its arrears, as per law, within a period of one month from the date of submission of such affidavit.
13.
Accordingly, writ petition stands disposed-off.
